events.subject: Welcome to nights
body: Your first week. Three things: write everything down, never search anyone, and call me if you are not sure.
The Field Manual in your notebook grows with every case. Read it.

events.subject: Marisol
events.body: Marisol told me how you handled 1412. Thank you for treating her fairly. I have already reminded the whole team about doors on trolleys.

events.subject: Your reports
events.body: Your 1412 report runs to two pages for a laptop that was never stolen. Night officers patrol; they do not write novels. Cut it down.

choices.label: Reply that every finding is referenced, and copy Desmond Okafor
choices.outcome: Desmond backs you in one line: "Keep writing them like that." Colm does not reply.

choices.label: Promise to keep future reports shorter
choices.outcome: Colm is pleased. Your next report leaves out the custody references, and Desmond sends it back.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.outcome: Colm takes the silence as agreement and complains about you at the supervisors' meeting.

events.subject: Last night at the Lobby Bar
body: The gentleman from your bar is awake and talking. The AED was on him and shocking before we were through the door, and your staff had the lift held. That is what saves people.
Whoever trained your bar team on the AED: keep doing it.

events.subject: Claim TM-55102
events.body: Thank you for the preserved footage. Our counsel would like a copy before the 30th. I understand you have a release policy; what do you need from us?

choices.label: Send the footage release form and route it to Desmond Okafor for approval
choices.outcome: The request comes back signed. Desmond approves the release with counsel, and the adjuster notes how cleanly it was handled.

choices.label: Email the clip to the adjuster yourself
choices.outcome: Counsel hears that footage left LP without approval. Desmond asks you to his office.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.outcome: The adjuster chases twice, then writes to the General Manager.

events.subject: Supervisor
body: You run the night shift now. Ines and the Tessmore guards report to you, and you will be audited on keys and doors, not only on cases.
Two habits: read the alarm log every week, and never let anyone fear telling you they lost a key.

events.subject: Thank you
events.body: Lucia got us the soft wrist coils. Everyone on my floor wears them now. Thank you for telling them it was not my fault.

events.subject: Bread deliveries
events.body: Chef tells me deliveries now need an LP officer at the dock. It is slowing the morning. Can we go back to the old way until the intercom is in?

choices.label: Explain the theft and keep the door shut; offer a fixed delivery window with an officer standing by
choices.outcome: Rafael grumbles, then agrees once he sees the clip. The bakery moves to 05:00.

choices.label: Agree to let the clerk prop it for ten minutes
choices.outcome: The door is propped again within a week. The alarm log fills up.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.outcome: Rafael takes it to the General Manager as LP being unhelpful.

events.subject: My case
events.body: The police found my case at the ferry terminal, without the laptop but with my mother's watch. Thank you for getting them there so fast, and for being honest with me that morning.
events.headline: Harbourfront thief stopped at the ferry terminal

events.subject: E-77
body: The vendor confirms E-77 is a genuine portable encoder from a batch sold to another hotel group two years ago and reported stolen. DS Calloway is interested.
Thirty-one keys in nineteen nights, and a man in a grey cap who knew where the trolleys stand. Somebody is shopping in our building. Keep your notebook close.

fallout.description: A weak call in "{mission}" comes back: {choice}. A guest complaint follows and the file does not hold up.
A theft claim on another floor goes badly. The investigation repeats a habit from "{mission}" ({choice}) and the guest's lawyer asks for the file.
Someone talks their way into a room that is not theirs, the way the gap in "{mission}" allowed ({choice}).
A guest dispute escalates on the floor. Staff repeat the approach from "{mission}" ({choice}) and a complaint reaches the brand.
A guest collapses in the spa. Staff repeat the approach from "{mission}" ({choice}) and the response is minutes slower than it should be.
Another unattended bag turns up at the ballroom. The team handles it the way "{mission}" went ({choice}) and the evening is disrupted for nothing, or not taken seriously enough.
Footage a claimant needed is gone or cannot be verified, the way "{mission}" went ({choice}). The insurer pays out and asks questions.
A key control gap from "{mission}" ({choice}) is still open when someone tries the same door again.
A back door is found propped again, the habit left from "{mission}" ({choice}). Stock goes missing from receiving.
The bell stand releases another bag on a name and a number, the gap from "{mission}" ({choice}). The guest's lawyer writes to the GM.
